title: Email service failure
text:
Title: Email service failure

Description: ### Severity
High

### Problem Summary
The email notification service failed when attempting to send an email notification, resulting in unhandled email sending errors.

### Impact
Users will not receive automated email notifications, transactional messages, or system alerts, causing communication breakdowns and potential operational disruptions.

### Possible Root Cause
- Invalid or expired SMTP credentials / API key configuration.
- Outbound network connectivity issues or firewall blocking SMTP/HTTP ports to the email provider.
- Service outage or rate limiting imposed by the email service provider.

### Error Log
```
2026-08-18 11:00:05 INFO Email notification requested
2026-08-18 11:00:06 ERROR Email service failed
2026-08-18 11:00:06 ERROR Unable to send notification email
2026-08-18 11:00:06 ERROR Email notification request failed
```

### Recommended Action
1. Verify email service / SMTP server credentials and environment configuration.
2. Check network logs and outgoing firewall rules for connections to the email provider.
3. Review email service provider status and error logs for rate limits or outage indicators.
4. Test email dispatch manually and implement retry logic for transient failures.

State: open

Labels: severity:high

title: Login button is not working
text:
Title: Login button is not working

Description: **Describe the bug**
Clicking the login button on the authentication page does not trigger any action. The user remains on the login page and no error message or network request appears to be initiated.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Navigate to the login page.
2. Enter valid user credentials.
3. Click on the "Login" button.

**Expected Behavior**
The user should be authenticated and redirected to the dashboard, or an appropriate error message should be displayed if authentication fails.

**Actual Behavior**
Nothing happens when clicking the login button.

**Environment / Context**
- Browser: All major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
- Device: Desktop / Mobile
